title: House fire - burns + smoke inhalation
objectives: Suspect CO despite SpO2 98%; 100% O2 by NRB (2.25)
Recognize airway burn signs; early airway alert + intercept, no delay (4.0)
Rule of nines: ~23% partial thickness; exclude 1st degree (4.0)
Stop burning, dry cover, prevent hypothermia; no prolonged cooling
2 large-bore IVs, warm LR 500 mL/hr (4.0); direct to UVMMC
resources: O2/NRB, BVM, suction, capno, SpCO (CO-oximeter) if carried, dry sterile sheets, blankets, IV x2, warm LR, albuterol. UVMMC (Level 1; no burn center in VT) ~10 min; intercept ETA 12 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to 41 Pheasant Way, South Burlington, for a working structure fire. Fire reports one occupant removed from the house with burns. Time out 0615.

scene.location: Front lawn of single-family home, 0620, dark, 24 F. ~10 min from UVMMC. Fire knocked down.
scene.setup: FD carried pt out of smoky kitchen 2 min ago. Pt sitting on a tarp. FD put a nasal cannula on him at 2 L.
scene.moulage: Soot on face/nares, singed brows, blistered R arm + upper chest + back of L hand, red L forearm; charred wet shirt; watch on R wrist.
scene.roles: Pt actor; FD lieutenant ("His sat's 98, he's good"); wife (got out unhurt, gives history).

patient.name: Robert Gagnon
patient.on_arrival: Sitting on tarp, coughing, hoarse, soot on face. Blistered R arm/chest. Unsure what time it is.

SAMPLE: Burning pain, headache, nausea, cough, "throat scratchy"
Grease fire ~0555; beat at it, shirt caught. ~10 min in smoky kitchen
OPQRST: R arm, chest, face, L hand

primary: Patent but **hoarse**; soot in mouth, singed nasal hairs
RR 26, cough, black-flecked sputum, scattered wheezes
Radial strong, rapid. Unburned skin warm
Stop burning, cut off smoldering shirt, remove watch. Cover, keep warm
secondary: Soot on tongue, singed nares; no swelling yet
Back of hand blistered (~1%); forearm red only (exclude)
**~23% partial thickness** (do not count red-only skin)

vitals.trigger: IF burns wet/cooled > 15 min or left uncovered
IF left on NC because SpO2 98% (~T+8)

vitals.other: Warm LR 500 mL/hr x2 lines. Hoarse, no stridor (unless D used)

flow.give: Read dispatch. FD Lt: "His sat's 98 on the cannula, he's good."
expected: Roles assigned; pt into warm rig early

flow.give: Stage **A**. Show MOUTH / THROAT card. SpCO card only if CO-oximeter used.

branches.then: no airway pre-alert; debrief when Stage **D** hits

expected: Airway burn signs named: soot, singed nares, hoarse, sputum (4.0)
Albuterol 2.5 mg neb w/ O2 for wheezes (2.25)

flow.give: Show BURNS card. Wife: "Get the hose, put cold water on it!"

branches.then: TBSA overcalled (~27%); debrief rule of nines

expected: TBSA ~23% partial thickness by rule of nines (4.0)
Dry sterile sheets, blankets, heat on (4.0)

flow.give: FD Lt: "Want the helicopter for a burn?" UVMMC 10 min; intercept 12 min.

branches.if: Waits on scene for intercept or air

expected: Direct to UVMMC (Level 1; no VT burn center)
Notify early: inhalation injury, TBSA, SpCO
Intercept en route only, no delay

flow.give: IV hard (R arm burned). Pt asks for "something for the pain."

branches.then: Stage **D**; expect upright, NRB, BVM + suction ready, Med Direction, UVMMC airway alert, no stop
debrief 4.0 rate 500 mL/hr; look for other shock cause

expected: Pain: IV acetaminophen (2.20A); opioids via intercept
Report: TBSA, airway signs, SpCO, time in smoke
SIREN: burn diagram, O2 start time

critical: O2 not maximized because SpO2 normal (2.25)
Airway burn signs missed / no early airway alert (4.0)
TBSA not estimated or 1st degree counted (4.0)
Large-area wet cooling or no hypothermia prevention (4.0)
Scene delay for intercept/air with UVMMC 10 min (8.0)
< 2 IVs or wrong fluid plan for > 20% TBSA (4.0)
Nitrous with AMS / paramedic meds given by AEMT (2.20A)
Watch/jewelry left on circumferential arm burn
differentials: BP high, improving on O2; intercept if worse
debrief: Which findings told you the airway was burned?
How did you get your TBSA, and what did you exclude?
Why not cool these burns with the hose?
Where should he go, and does air help? What fluid rate?

crew_card.dispatch: 41 Pheasant Way, South Burlington. Working structure fire, FD removed one occupant with burns. 0615, dark, 24 F.
crew_card.on_arrival: Fire knocked down. Man in his 60s sitting on a tarp on the lawn, coughing, face black with soot, R sleeve burned off. FD has a nasal cannula on him.

actor_card.Act: Cough often, hoarse raspy voice. Rub your head: "My head is pounding."
actor_card.Confusion: Unsure of time/day. Ask "Is Linda out?" twice.
actor_card.Airway swelling (on cue): Noisy high-pitched breathing in, muffled voice, sit forward, drool.
actor_card.Wife (Linda): "Get the hose on him!" Gives meds/history when asked.

show_cards.title: MOUTH / THROAT
show_cards.body:
Soot on tongue and in nostrils.
Nose hairs singed.
Voice hoarse.
Coughing black-flecked sputum.

show_cards.title: BURNS
show_cards.body:
Face: forehead/cheeks red, blistered; brows singed.
R arm: blistered, wet, shoulder to fingers, all the way around. Watch on wrist.
Upper front chest: blistered.
Back of L hand: blistered.
L forearm: red, no blisters.

show_cards.title: PULSE CO-OXIMETER
show_cards.cue: Only if crew uses a CO-oximeter (Stage A). Stage B: SpCO 19%. Stage E: SpCO 26%

show_cards.title: 12-LEAD
show_cards.caption: Sinus tachycardia. Otherwise normal ECG.
show_cards.cue: Stage A (2.25: acquire + transmit). Machine read only

moulage_tags.cue: Stage D: add stridor, muffled voice

moulage_tags.text: Blistered, wet, shoulder to fingers, all the way around; watch on wrist
